remaining: Local tests cannot establish every packaged platform or published asset. Protected validation and release checks remain required.
evidenceDecision: Real packaging/installer/release/CI tests exercise archive validation and dependency gates; actual platform/release workflows supply distribution evidence. Upstream-sync tests directly enumerate bounded repair/authority cases and reconstruct conflicting Git merges with exact ancestry and binary patches; hosted App eligibility, model quality and API execution remain platform evidence (docs/upstream-automation.md). Proposed installer-upgrade CI builds real native candidate archives and exercises latest-stable plugin installation, authenticated runtime/session migration and failed-checksum retention in isolated state. This direct platform evidence is more useful than a model of OS packaging; Older release combinations beyond the frozen previous release remain excluded (docs/release.md). OpenSpec notes source admission and public feature rendering use direct filesystem/Markdown/link regressions; Pages workflow checks cover build inputs and test wiring. Native OpenSpec owns agent discovery; no repository lookup remains. These static transformations introduce no ordering or recovery state, so direct build and policy checks are more useful than an additional model; synchronous OpenSpec batch archives use real Git and the pinned CLI to cover merge-date ordering, incomplete tasks, successful-prefix retention and restored conflict boundaries. Archive-helper fixtures cover reviewed preparation without automatic main publication; hosted execution and review remain platform evidence. The feature-map repair additionally checks the complete tracked-source baseline, deleted-source admission without weakening spec deletion policy, the real legacy archive baseline and visible empty-batch failures. Release-please, GitHub Release and Homebrew PR state belong to standard actions. Commit-qualified release-please label fixtures cover pending/tagged retries, consecutive releases, absent/ambiguous/wrong-base identities and API/edit refusal; graph checks cover retained-artifact skips through every publisher and the label job, and real summary execution rejects every skipped/failed/cancelled publication stage. Windows plugin fixtures reuse the actual marked manifest; a Linux regression applies the actual PowerShell version pattern to it, with native Windows execution retained as platform evidence. Workflow graph checks require tag-only native builds, every native install/upgrade/walk/audit before the immutable artifact, and serialized standard publishers consuming that exact artifact. Shell-step subprocess fixtures cover idempotent existing-byte/integrity checks and refusing conflicts; the tap's standard PR action applies the exact four-platform Formula after mislav opens its single-URL proposal, reusing the same open PR on rerun. Linux-only required checks retry only failed unit files or exact browser cases once in the same job, never making a second failure green; models and other checks never retry. Real runner subprocess fixtures cover scope and missing/crashed/isolation-failed evidence. Exhaustive four-event histories cover distinct-run counting, reordered completion, seven-day boundaries and explicit quarantine. Mock GitHub API tests cover lost create replies, idempotent updates, closed fixes, stale verdicts and trusted pending/final statuses. Workflow graph tests require default-branch-only serialized issue writes and read-only candidate jobs. Hosted GitHub statuses, permissions and artifact delivery remain platform evidence. Main reports identical immutable PR evidence without starting heavy jobs; absent evidence remains red. Nightly exercises native regressions and running upgrades as advisory signal. Native channel checks launch the exact packages, preserve data through running installer/Homebrew upgrades and restart after old-keg deletion. The standard artifact identity/digest binds publication to this tag run; expired artifacts force full acceptance. These real workflow/platform boundaries are more direct than an abstract model of externally owned registries. Release dispatch subprocess fixtures execute the workflow shell against the actual manifest config, checking exact RC/final overrides, an omitted flag with always-bump-patch configured for default patch increments, explicit minor overrides, invalid-input refusal and automatic same-repository PR checks. Workflow graph assertions scope the tap token to the Homebrew job in the tag-only release environment and retain npm OIDC without an environment. The pinned upstream CLI dry run checks real manifest version selection; the tag-plan fixture accepts RC1, RC2 and final in sequence. These are deterministic CLI/config transformations rather than an additional ownership state machine. Hosted token/ruleset/registry/tap operation and RC rehearsal remain platform acceptance. Merge-queue workflow graph checks bind checks_requested to the existing Linux Delivery checks aggregate, event-SHA checkout and immutable queue base. A real scope-selector subprocess traps all GitHub evidence requests and requires a full active selection for merge_group even with PR context present; the event branch excludes every PR reuse/hold path. Side-workflow inventory checks prevent unintended queue subscribers. GitHub owns queue ordering, reconstruction, review enforcement and merging; hosted ruleset behavior remains platform acceptance, so no local model of the external queue is added. Dependabot description admission is a stateless GitHub event identity predicate: direct tests exhaust the sender/author login and type equivalence classes, retain ordinary impact requirements and file-based test selection, and exercise exact metadata exceptions, commit/file privacy failures and redacted diagnostics through the real checker. No additional ordering model is needed; a green unedited hosted Dependabot PR remains platform acceptance.
